title: Neutral-citation token-boundary parity between the NEW2 ingest extractor and every API canonicalization path

rootCause.mechanism: The word boundary sits AFTER the optional -DB/-FB group. On "2025:DHC:8491-DBThis", B followed by T is not a word boundary, so the -DB alternative fails; the group is optional so it matches EMPTY, and the trailing \b then succeeds at the position after 8491, because a digit followed by a hyphen IS a boundary. The regex never errors — it returns a different, valid-looking citation key.
rootCause.note: This is the SAME regex NEW2 R18 fixed in services/ingest/src/harvest/hc-load.ts. R18 deliberately left this second copy: changing it moves judgment_citations.normalised_citation, i.e. the edge key space, while CITATION_BULK_APPLY = HOLD.

parityMatrix.PARITY_DISAGREEMENTS_AFTER_NOTE: UNCHANGED BY THIS ROUND, AND DELIBERATELY. The single shared extractor is NEW2-owned and NEW2 held it on purpose. LCC has no independent parser to correct, and duplicating one is forbidden by query-shape.ts's own contract.

documentedLayerDifferences.ingest: null (neutralCitationFrom REFUSES when the page prints two)
documentedLayerDifferences.api: 2025:DHC:8491-DB (extractCitations returns both; the classifier takes the first)
documentedLayerDifferences.verdict: NOT A DEFECT. neutralCitationFrom answers 'what is THIS document's own citation'; extractCitations answers 'what citations appear in this text'. Forcing byte identity would make search refuse valid queries or make ingest guess an identity it cannot prove.

proposedFixValidatedInIsolation.method: The R18 boundary was applied to an ISOLATED COPY of services/ingest/src/citations.ts in a scratch directory and run beside the committed module over the frozen control set. The tracked file was never modified.
proposedFixValidatedInIsolation.verdict: The one-line boundary move closes every LCC parity hole and moves nothing else on this control set. Handed to NEW2 as evidence; NEW2 owns the write because it moves the edge key space.

canonicalJudgmentCitations.note: judgments.neutral_citation is written by hc-load.ts, NOT by the defective extractor. Already NEW2 R18's frozen population. Out of LCC scope.

resolvedCitationEdges.honestBound: 1,159,919 is an UPPER BOUND, not an estimate. citation_text stores the regex's own match[0], already truncated, and evidence is NULL on all 1,376,237 neutral rows - so the glue is NOT recoverable from the edge row. The only deterministic in-database signal is the 83 split pairs / 158 corpus-wide split citations, and even those include genuine cases where a court printed both forms. Settling the true figure requires re-reading source text, which is NEW2's population walk, not LCC's.

aliases.why: Migration 0027: CHECK (alias_reporter IN ('AIR','SCC')). Not a sample - a constraint. A neutral citation cannot be an alias row.

judgmentCitationKeys.note: neutralEndingDbFb matches judgments.neutral_citation exactly (210,791 both sides), confirming this table is a faithful mirror of hc-load's output and carries no independent exposure.

citationChecks.note: citation_checks is an append-only audit of what was SHOWN to a user. Not a key space to correct, and not rewritable.

separateFindings.finding: The PD-7 lock cannot see a High Court neutral citation at all. Measured: extractCitationSpans('2025:DHC:8491-DB') === [], and the same for the plain and glued forms. Its own comment says 'This function IS the PD-7 lock, so a form it cannot see is a citation the advocate can edit or remove without the server raising a 422' - the false negative it calls the dangerous direction.
separateFindings.whyNotFixedHere: It is a coverage gap, not a token-boundary parity defect. Fixing it broadens citation syntax on a user-facing integrity surface, which this round's instructions forbid doing on guesswork, and it needs its own evidence and its own failure-first test.
separateFindings.recommendation: Own LCC round. Reuse the frozen control set in this artifact.

separateFindings.finding: Same four shapes, same blindness: a model-generated High Court neutral citation is not stripped from generated text. Measured: stripInventedCitations('2025:DHC:8491-DB') returns the string unchanged.
separateFindings.whyNotFixedHere: Same reason as F2, and the two should be corrected together since they are the same closed set written twice.

finalState.RESOLVER_READY_REASON: The round's own bar requires that no known parser divergence remains in currently exercised citation paths. Three remain, in the shared NEW2-owned extractor, and they are exercised by /search on every bare-citation query. The suffix defect is therefore reproduced and located but NOT corrected, because the only correct correction is a NEW2 write.
